notes.text: This queue IS the batch record; there is no batch.yaml, matching BATCH-51e2aa in this goal, which also has none. The opening decision is DEC-20260915-428a17 and the human-readable account is opening-report.md beside this file.

A second lane on GOAL-ICPERF-e6b6a4 -- H-ICPERF-5f038b / EXP-ICPERF-025a52, descent as a DAG -- is driven by another session from its own branch. Its current state, read here through the merge digest rather than assumed: DEC-20260915-d8d413 (merged to main as 851c19411) decided `revise` and WITHHELD approval, so that contract sits at `draft` / approved_by null, and `tools/goal_lanes.py lanes GOAL-ICPERF-e6b6a4` records no lane. It may resume at any point during this batch without this session being told, which is the ordinary condition here and the reason this batch is built disjoint from it either way: no task here reads or writes that hypothesis, that experiment directory, or coordination/goals/GOAL-ICPERF-e6b6a4/tasks/TASK-20260915-532164/, so a session resuming the descent lane mid-batch collides with nothing but the goal head, which each edits additively inside its own archive (docs/concurrent-goal-lanes.md). CORR-20260915-6708e4 records a dispatch-precondition violation against that lane; every producing card here carries explicit dispatch_preconditions in response.

Every archive in this batch declares binding_mode content_at_commit, which verifies declared path hashes in the archive's own commit rather than at HEAD (CORR-20260915-654160). This batch is the first to be designed that way and it is the right default here: the package of a batch that repairs an instrument contains records that MUST move afterwards -- a contract advancing to `completed`, a draft contract to `approved`, a goal head reranked at every checkpoint.
